paragraphs.title: Nehemiah's Request to the King and Preparations for the Journey

easy.explanation: Nehemiah took up the wine and gave it to the king.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah give to the king?

easy.explanation: Jerusalem, the place of his fathers' sepulchres, lay waste and its gates were burned.

answers: Go to Judah and rebuild the city
easy.explanation: Nehemiah asked to be sent to Judah so that he might build the city.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah ask the king to let him do?

answers: He prayed to the God of heaven
medium.explanation: Before answering, Nehemiah prayed to the God of heaven.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah do before answering the king's request?

medium.explanation: The letters were official documents for the governors beyond the river.
medium.q: In the phrase “let letters be given me,” what does “letters” mean?

answers: To make beams for gates, the wall, and a house
medium.explanation: Nehemiah requested timber for several building projects in Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah ask for timber from the king?

answers: As the good hand of his God
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah said the king granted his requests according to the good hand of his God upon him.
challenge.q: How did Nehemiah understand the king's favorable response?

answers: It was a serious and dangerous conversation
He wanted to cancel the journey
challenge.explanation: The text says, “Then I was very sore afraid.”
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah's fear show about speaking to the king?

answers: He requested timber, prayed, and described Jerusalem
He described Jerusalem, prayed, and asked to go to Judah
He went to Judah, requested permission, and then described the city
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah described Jerusalem's condition, prayed, and then asked permission to go and rebuild.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Nehemiah's actions?

paragraphs.title: The Journey to Jerusalem and Opposition from the Enemies

easy.explanation: Nehemiah came to the governors beyond the river and gave them the king's letters.
easy.q: To whom did Nehemiah give the king's letters?

answers: Captains of the army and horsemen
easy.explanation: The king sent captains of the army and horsemen with Nehemiah.
easy.q: Who accompanied Nehemiah on his journey?

easy.explanation: They were exceedingly grieved that Nehemiah had come to seek the welfare of Israel.
easy.q: How did Sanballat and Tobiah react to Nehemiah's arrival?

medium.explanation: They were the authorities whom Nehemiah met on his way to Judah.
medium.q: In this passage, what were the “governors beyond the river”?

answers: Nehemiah sought the welfare of the children of Israel
medium.explanation: They were grieved because a man had come to seek the welfare of the Israelites.
medium.q: Why were Sanballat and Tobiah angry?

answers: He was going to war in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The king sent the military escort with Nehemiah, along with the king's letters.
medium.q: What can be inferred from the army captains and horsemen accompanying Nehemiah?

answers: The king helps Nehemiah, but Sanballat and Tobiah oppose him
The king is angry, but the people rejoice
Nehemiah hides the journey from the king
challenge.explanation: The king supports Nehemiah's journey, while the opposing officials are distressed.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in these verses?

answers: To seek the welfare of the Israelites
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Nehemiah came to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
challenge.q: What was Nehemiah's purpose according to the enemies' reaction?

answers: They show him carrying out the approved journey
They show that the approval was canceled
They describe the wall being completed
challenge.explanation: After receiving permission, letters, and an escort, Nehemiah traveled toward Jerusalem.
challenge.q: How do these verses relate to Nehemiah's request to the king?

paragraphs.title: The Secret Night Inspection of Jerusalem

easy.explanation: Nehemiah says, “So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.”
easy.q: How long was Nehemiah in Jerusalem before the inspection?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah arose and went out by night.
easy.q: When did Nehemiah go out to inspect the city?

easy.explanation: He went out with some few men.

medium.explanation: The walls had been broken down, leaving openings and destruction.
medium.q: What does “broken down” mean when describing Jerusalem's walls?

medium.explanation: He had not yet told anyone what God had put in his heart to do.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah go out with only a few men at night?

medium.explanation: He viewed the walls of Jerusalem and its gates, which had been consumed with fire.

answers: He carefully investigated before announcing the plan
He did not know the city's condition
challenge.explanation: He first examined the situation privately and had not yet told the leaders or people.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah's secrecy reveal about his approach?

answers: There was no place for his beast to pass
The city had no gates at all
challenge.explanation: At the king's pool, there was no place for the beast under him to pass.
challenge.q: What practical difficulty did Nehemiah encounter?

answers: No beast was with him except the one he rode
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah specifically says that no beast was with him except the one he rode upon.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes that the inspection party was small?

paragraphs.title: The Call to Rebuild Jerusalem's Wall

answers: The city lay waste and the gates were burned
A royal palace had been built
easy.explanation: Nehemiah described the distress, ruin, and burned gates of Jerusalem.
easy.q: What condition did Nehemiah describe in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: He said, “Come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem.”
easy.q: What did Nehemiah ask the leaders to do?

answers: They agreed and strengthened themselves to work
easy.explanation: They said, “Let us rise up and build,” and strengthened their hands for the good work.
easy.q: How did the people respond to Nehemiah's appeal?

medium.explanation: Rebuilding the wall would remove Jerusalem's shame and disgrace.
medium.q: What does “reproach” mean in this passage?

answers: About God's good hand and the king's words
About treasures found in the city
medium.explanation: Nehemiah told them about God's help and the king's authorization.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah tell the people to encourage them?

answers: The ruined walls and burned gates needed to be restored
The wall was needed to enlarge the palace
medium.explanation: The destruction of the walls and gates created the need for rebuilding.
medium.q: Why did Jerusalem's condition lead to a call to rebuild?

answers: To show divine help and royal authorization
To announce that the king opposed him
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah connected God's good hand with the king's approval of the work.
challenge.q: Why did Nehemiah mention both God's help and the king's words?

answers: The discovery of a new gate
challenge.explanation: After hearing about the city's distress and the help Nehemiah received, they decided to build.
challenge.q: What moved the people from recognizing the problem to taking action?

answers: That they would no longer be a reproach
That they would obtain more timber
That they would reach the king's palace
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah wanted Jerusalem to be no more a reproach.
challenge.q: What additional purpose did Nehemiah give for rebuilding?

paragraphs.title: Mockery from the Enemies and Nehemiah's Reply

answers: The king and the army captains
easy.explanation: These three opponents laughed the Jews to scorn and despised them.
They asked, “Will ye rebel against the king?”
easy.q: Of what did the enemies accuse the Jews?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah said, “The God of heaven, he will prosper us.”
easy.q: In whom did Nehemiah say they trusted?

answers: A share or right of participation
medium.explanation: Nehemiah denied that the enemies had any share, right, or memorial in Jerusalem.
medium.q: What does “portion” mean in Nehemiah's statement to the enemies?

answers: He answered with faith and confidence
medium.explanation: He declared that God would prosper them and that His servants would arise and build.
medium.q: How did Nehemiah answer the accusation of rebellion?

answers: Nehemiah had royal authorization for the work
The king had forbidden the work
Nehemiah did not mention the king's approval
medium.explanation: The king had granted permission, so the accusation that the work was unauthorized was false.
medium.q: How do the king's words relate to Nehemiah's answer?

answers: God will prosper the work, and the enemies have no right in Jerusalem
The enemies should build in his place
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah expressed confidence in God's help and rejected the enemies' claim to Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What is the main point of Nehemiah's answer to the enemies?

answers: The enemies speak of rebellion, while Nehemiah speaks of God's work and building
The enemies want to build, while Nehemiah wants to destroy
The enemies speak of prayer, while Nehemiah speaks of mockery
challenge.explanation: The enemies describe the work as rebellion, but Nehemiah identifies the builders as God's servants.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the enemies' words and Nehemiah's words?

answers: He remained committed and did not surrender to mockery
He hid the enemies' words from the people
challenge.explanation: Despite the mockery and accusation, Nehemiah declared that they would arise and build.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah's response show about his attitude toward opposition?
